scenes.heading: Introduction to Network Layers
bullets: OSI model organizes networking into 7 distinct layers
TCP/IP model condenses this architecture into 4 layers
Each layer provides services to the layer immediately above it
scenes.narration: Computer networks rely on layered architectures so that hardware, protocols, and user applications can communicate seamlessly without needing to know low-level implementation details.
scenes.visual_hint: Side-by-side comparison diagram showing the 7 OSI layers and the 4 TCP/IP layers

checkpoint.q: How many layers comprise the standard OSI reference model?

scenes.heading: Physical and Data Link Transmission
bullets: Physical layer transmits raw bits across physical media
Data Link layer frames bits and handles hop-to-hop delivery
Uses hardware MAC addresses for local subnet routing
scenes.narration: At the lowest level, bits travel across fiber, copper, or radio frequencies. The Data Link layer packages these raw bits into structured frames with header check sequences to spot transmission errors.
scenes.visual_hint: Diagram of an Ethernet frame showing preamble, source MAC, destination MAC, and payload

checkpoint.q: Which address type operates at the Data Link layer?

scenes.heading: Network Layer: Logical Addressing and Routing
bullets: IP protocol manages global host-to-host addressing
Routers inspect destination IP addresses to forward packets
IPv4 uses 32-bit addresses while IPv6 utilizes 128-bit addresses
scenes.narration: The Network layer moves packets across multiple networks. Routers check routing tables to forward each packet along the optimal path across the internet until reaching the destination subnet.
scenes.visual_hint: Router forwarding packets between networks using routing table lookups

checkpoint.q: How many bits are in a standard IPv4 address?

scenes.heading: Transport Layer: Reliable End-to-End Delivery
bullets: Provides process-to-process communication using port numbers
TCP provides reliable, connection-oriented data streaming
UDP provides lightweight, connectionless datagram delivery
scenes.narration: While IP gets packets to the right machine, the Transport layer ensures data reaches the specific running application. TCP guarantees in-order arrival, retransmitting any lost packets automatically.
scenes.visual_hint: Transport layer multiplexing data from Web, Email, and DNS processes to separate port numbers

checkpoint.q: Which transport protocol guarantees in-order, reliable packet arrival?

scenes.heading: Throughput and Bandwidth Calculations
bullets: Bandwidth represents raw theoretical channel capacity (bps)
Throughput measures actual successfully transmitted data rate
Latency measures total one-way transit delay across the link
scenes.narration: For university exam numerical problems, always differentiate bandwidth from throughput. Throughput is bottlenecked by network congestion, protocol overhead, and packet loss.
scenes.visual_hint: Visual pipe analogy contrasting total bandwidth diameter with actual fluid throughput flow

checkpoint.q: What term denotes the actual rate of successful data transfer across a network?

scenes.heading: Application Layer & Exam Synthesis
bullets: Direct interface for user applications (HTTP, DNS, SSH)
Encapsulation appends headers at each descending layer
Decapsulation strips headers at each ascending layer
scenes.narration: At the top sits the Application layer. Remember the complete journey: data is encapsulated with protocol headers down the stack, transmitted across media, and decapsulated up the destination stack.
scenes.visual_hint: Summary animation showing data encapsulation down sender stack and decapsulation up receiver stack

checkpoint.q: What is the process of adding protocol headers as data moves down the stack called?
